title: Practice: «To begin doing»: за- and others

blocks.text: Sentences and their English: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR). Words, meanings and how each word is built: the English Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0).

exercises.why: **заговорил** — заговори́ть (perfective): to begin to speak; to talk someone's ear off (tire someone out by one's talk); to exorcise, to bewitch, to charm, to cast a spell, to enchant. Wiktionary: за- + говори́ть.
exercises.context: The English says which word it is.

exercises.q: I was the first to begin speaking.
exercises.why: **заговорил** — заговори́ть (perfective): to begin to speak; to talk someone's ear off (tire someone out by one's talk); to exorcise, to bewitch, to charm, to cast a spell, to enchant. Wiktionary: за- + говори́ть.
exercises.context: The English says which word it is.

exercises.why: **рассмеялся** — рассмея́ться (perfective): to burst out laughing, to start laughing. Wiktionary: рас- + смея́ться.
exercises.context: The English says which word it is.

exercises.q: Match each word with its meaning (Wiktionary's definitions).
pairs: to begin to shout, to cry out, to give a shout
to start running, to break into a run
exercises.why: From Wiktionary: заговори́ть — to begin to speak; закрича́ть — to begin to shout, to cry out, to give a shout; засмея́ться — to laugh, to start laughing; побежа́ть — to start running, to break into a run.

exercises.q: Tom was the first one to laugh.
exercises.why: **рассмеялся** — рассмея́ться (perfective): to burst out laughing, to start laughing. Wiktionary: рас- + смея́ться.
exercises.context: The English says which word it is.

exercises.why: **поплыл** — поплы́ть (perfective): to start swimming, to start floating; to start sailing; (figuratively) to hesitate or be unsure; (colloquial, slang, figuratively) to lose one's nerve. Wiktionary: по- + плыть.
exercises.context: The English says which word it is.

exercises.why: **поплывёт** — поплы́ть (perfective): to start swimming, to start floating; to start sailing; (figuratively) to hesitate or be unsure; (colloquial, slang, figuratively) to lose one's nerve. Wiktionary: по- + плыть.
exercises.context: The English says which word it is.

exercises.q: Match each word with its meaning (Wiktionary's definitions).
pairs: to begin to want, to begin to desire
to start singing, to sing out
to begin to tremble, to begin to shiver
exercises.why: From Wiktionary: захоте́ть — to begin to want, to begin to desire; запла́кать — to start crying, weeping; запе́ть — to start singing, to sing out; задрожа́ть — to begin to tremble, to begin to shiver.

exercises.q: Match each word with its meaning (Wiktionary's definitions).
pairs: to burst out laughing, to start laughing
to start smoking, to light up
exercises.why: From Wiktionary: рассмея́ться — to burst out laughing, to start laughing; закури́ть — to start smoking, to light up; зарабо́тать — to earn; заигра́ть — to begin to play.

exercises.q: Match each word with its meaning (Wiktionary's definitions).
pairs: (colloquial) to burst out laughing, to roar with laughter
exercises.why: From Wiktionary: забе́гать — to start running; расхохота́ться — (colloquial) to burst out laughing, to roar with laughter; загреме́ть — to begin to thunder; заинтересова́ть — to (start to) interest, to concern.

exercises.q: Match each word with its meaning (Wiktionary's definitions).
pairs: to begin to sob/blubber, to burst out sobbing
to start muttering, to start mumbling
to start swimming, to start floating
exercises.why: From Wiktionary: зарыда́ть — to begin to sob/blubber, to burst out sobbing; забормота́ть — to start muttering, to start mumbling; потащи́ть — to start pulling; поплы́ть — to start swimming, to start floating.

exercises.q: Match each word with its meaning (Wiktionary's definitions).
pairs: to (begin to) howl, to raise a howl
exercises.why: From Wiktionary: завы́ть — to (begin to) howl, to raise a howl; зашепта́ть — to begin to whisper; зашага́ть — to begin to walk; застона́ть — to start moaning.

exercises.q: Match each word with its meaning (Wiktionary's definitions).
exercises.why: From Wiktionary: влете́ть — to fly into; заскрипе́ть — to begin to creak; опу́хнуть — to swell; возненави́деть — to hate, to start hating.
